Appendix

.1 Matrix Minors

Here we report key linear algebra identities that are used in the next sections of the Appendix for deriving the determinant sampling averages. These identities describe how to compute matrix minors, namely determinants of square submatrices, with their complementary minors of the inverse matrix. For an N×NN\times N matrix WW and a collection rows I=(i1,…,iM)I=(i_{1},\ldots,i_{M}) and columns J=(j1,…,jM)J=(j_{1},\ldots,j_{M}), let WI​JW_{I\,J} ( WI¯​J¯W_{\overline{I}\,\overline{J}} ) denote the M×MM\times M ((N−M)×(N−M)(N-M)\times(N-M)) submatrices given by selecting (removing) rows II and columns JJ. Additionally, WI​JW_{I\,J} is given so that the selected rows and columns are permuted to match orderings as given by II and JJ respectively. The minors of WW for removing rows II and columns JJ can be expressed in terms of the minors of WW for including rows JJ and columns II and the determinant of WW as

det⁡[WI¯​J¯]=±det⁡[(W−1)J​I]​det⁡[W].\det[W_{\overline{I}\,\overline{J}}]=\pm\det[(W^{-1})_{J\,I}]\,\det[W]. (32)

When rows and columns are normally ordered as i1<i2<…i_{1}<i_{2}<\ldots and j1<j2<…j_{1}<j_{2}<\ldots, the ±\pm sign is given by (−1)i1+j1+…+iM+jM(-1)^{i_{1}+j_{1}+\ldots+i_{M}+j_{M}}. For general orderings of II and JJ, as permutations of the normal orderings, the ±\pm sign is given by the signs of these two permutations. In the following sections of the Appendix, the identity will only be applied for the lowest cases of M=1M=1 or M=2M=2. In these scenarios, the identity can be expressed as

det⁡[Wi1¯​j1¯]\displaystyle\det[W_{\overline{i_{1}}\,\overline{j_{1}}}] =(−1)i1+j1​(W−1)j1​i1​det⁡[W]\displaystyle=(-1)^{i_{1}+j_{1}}\left(W^{-1}\right)_{j_{1}\,i_{1}}\,\det[W] (33)
det⁡[W(i1,i2)¯​(j1,j2)¯]\displaystyle\det[W_{\overline{(i_{1},i_{2})}\,\overline{(j_{1},j_{2})}}] =(−1)i1+j1+i2′+j2′​(W−1)j1​i1​((Wi1¯​j1¯)−1)j2′​i2′​det⁡[W],\displaystyle=(-1)^{i_{1}+j_{1}+i^{\prime}_{2}+j^{\prime}_{2}}\left(W^{-1}\right)_{j_{1}\,i_{1}}\left(\left(W_{\overline{i_{1}}\,\overline{j_{1}}}\right)^{-1}\right)_{j^{\prime}_{2}\,i^{\prime}_{2}}\,\det[W],

where the primed indices denote the new relative indices for the corresponding unprimed indices after removing other rows and columns. Therefore, we have that (Wi1¯​j1¯)i2′​j2′=Wi2​j2(W_{\overline{i_{1}}\overline{j_{1}}})_{i^{\prime}_{2}j^{\prime}_{2}}=W_{i_{2}j_{2}} which gives i2′=i2i^{\prime}_{2}=i_{2} (j2′=j2j^{\prime}_{2}=j_{2}) if i2<i1i_{2}<i_{1} (j2<j1j_{2}<j_{1}) and i2′=i2−1i^{\prime}_{2}=i_{2}-1 (j2′=j2−1j^{\prime}_{2}=j_{2}-1) if i2>i1i_{2}>i_{1} (j2>j1j_{2}>j_{1}).

In the derivations of the determinant sampling averages, Eq. 33 is applied repeatedly to the N×NN\times N overlap matrices Φ⁡(S)=[[⁡S|Φ​]]\Phi(S)=\lbb S|\Phi\rbb between the sampled NN-tuples SS and the variational basis states Φ\Phi. In this case of overlap matrices, the sub-matrix (Φ⁡(S))I¯​J¯(\Phi(S))_{\overline{I}\,\overline{J}} is then equivalent to the overlap matrix ΦJ¯​(SI¯)=[[⁡SI¯|ΦJ¯​]]\Phi_{\overline{J}}(S_{\overline{I}})=\lbb S_{\overline{I}}|\Phi_{\overline{J}}\rbb, where SI¯S_{\overline{I}} and ΦJ¯\Phi_{\overline{J}} denote the (N−MN-M)-tuples given by removing the states si1,…,siMs_{i_{1}},\ldots,s_{i_{M}} from SS and the states ϕj1,…,ϕjM\phi_{j_{1}},\ldots,\phi_{j_{M}} from Φ\Phi respectively. Importantly, this notation signifies that the minors det⁡[(Φ⁡(S))I¯​J¯]=det⁡[ΦJ¯​(SI¯)]\det[(\Phi(S))_{\overline{I}\overline{J}}]=\det[\Phi_{\overline{J}}(S_{\overline{I}})] are functionally independent of the MM states SI=(si1,…,siM)S_{I}=(s_{i_{1}},\ldots,s_{i_{M}}). The application of the identity Eq. 33 will allow the summations over SS to be factorized separately over SIS_{I} and SI¯S_{\overline{I}}, with the ladder terms given by a minor and a complex conjugate minor. From Eq. 4, a series of minors and conjugate minors of Φ⁡(S)\Phi(S) results in a corresponding Gram matrix minor as

∑S∈𝒮N−Mdet⁡[ΦI​(S)]∗​det​[ΦJ​(S)]=(N−M)!​det​[(G⁡(Φ))I¯​J¯].\displaystyle\sum_{S\in\mathcal{S}^{N-M}}\det[\Phi_{I}(S)]^{*}\det[\Phi_{J}(S)]=(N-M)!\,\det[\,(G(\Phi))_{\overline{I}\overline{J}}\,]. (34)

.2 Determinant Sampling Averages: One Local Matrix

Let us consider a general normalized overlap of the type ⟨ϕ|​|a⟩/⟨ϕ|​|ϕ⟩\bra{\phi}\ket{a}/\bra{\phi}\ket{\phi}. This includes the case of an expectation value when |a⟩=A^​|ϕ⟩\ket{a}=\hat{A}\ket{\phi}, for a given operator A^\hat{A}. For single-state VMC, the derivation of the average of the local estimator is straightforward. The ϕ⁡(s)=⟨s|ϕ⟩\phi(s)=\langle s|\phi\rangle from the probabilities cancels out the ϕ⁡(s)\phi(s) in the denominator of the local estimator, leaving the multiplication between ⟨s|a⟩\langle s|a\rangle and ⟨ϕ|s⟩\langle\phi|s\rangle in the numerator. Then, the summation over ss results in the overlap ⟨ϕ|a⟩\langle\phi|a\rangle normalized by ⟨ϕ|ϕ⟩\langle\phi|\phi\rangle. Now, for the determinant sampling averages of local matrix estimators, the ϕ⁡(s)\phi(s) from the probabilities become det⁡[Φ⁡(S)]\det[\Phi(S)] and the ϕ⁡(s)\phi(s) in the denominator become the inverse matrix Φ−1​(S)\Phi^{-1}(S). The local matrices are constructed as A~​(S)=Φ−1​(S)⋅A⁡(S)\widetilde{A}(S)=\Phi^{-1}(S)\cdot A(S), where A⁡(S)=[[⁡S|A​]]A(S)=\lbb S|A\rbb. Local operator matrices correspond to taking |A]]=A^|Φ]]|A\rbb=\hat{A}|\Phi\rbb, while local ratio matrices correspond to taking |A]]=|Ψ]]|A\rbb=|\Psi\rbb. The average of local matrices 𝔼⁡[A⁡(S)]=[[⁡Φ~|A​]]\Ex[A(S)]=\lbb\widetilde{\Phi}|A\rbb can be decomposed to give the more general averages:

𝔼⁡[(Φ−1​(S))ik​Akj​(S)]=1N​⟨ϕ~i|aj⟩.\displaystyle\Ex\left[\left(\Phi^{-1}(S)\right)_{ik}A_{kj}(S)\right]=\frac{1}{N}\langle\widetilde{\phi}_{i}|a_{j}\rangle. (35)

The key component of the derivation is that, instead of simply canceling, the identity Eq. 33 is applied transforming matrix determinants to matrix minors. Firstly, conjugated terms need to be inserted to match the unconjugated terms from the local matrices. In order to also apply the identity Eq. 33 to det⁡[Φ⁡(S)]∗\det[\Phi(S)]^{*} from the probabilities, conjugated Φ−1\Phi^{-1} matrix elements must be added. Then, the overlaps Ak​j​(S)=⟨sk|aj⟩A_{kj}(S)=\langle s_{k}|a_{j}\rangle from the local matrices must be paired with added overlaps Φk​ℓ∗​(S)=⟨ϕℓ|sk⟩\Phi^{*}_{k\ell}(S)=\langle\phi_{\ell}|s_{k}\rangle. Like for the single state VMC case, this will eventually allow the summations over sks_{k} to result in physical overlaps ⟨ϕℓ|aj⟩\langle\phi_{\ell}|a_{j}\rangle. Both of these needed additional terms are given by inserting the identity 1=(Φ⁡(S)⋅Φ−1​(S))k​k∗1=(\Phi(S)\cdot\Phi^{-1}(S))_{kk}^{*} into each term of the series. So, we obtain:

𝔼⁡[(Φ−1​(S))ik​Akj​(S)]\displaystyle\displaystyle\Ex\left[\left(\Phi^{-1}(S)\right)_{ik}A_{kj}(S)\right] =1N!​det⁡[G]​∑S∈𝒮N|det⁡[Φ⁡(S)]|2​(Φ−1​(S))i​k​Ak​j​(S)\displaystyle=\frac{1}{N!\det[G]}\sum_{S\in\mathcal{S}^{N}}|\det[\Phi(S)]|^{2}\left(\Phi^{-1}(S)\right)_{ik}A_{kj}(S)
=1N!​det⁡[G]∑S∈𝒮N(``")(∑ℓ=1NΦk​ℓ(S)(Φ−1(S))ℓ​k)∗⋅\displaystyle=\frac{1}{N!\det[G]}\sum_{S\in\mathcal{S}^{N}}\Biggl(``\quad"\Biggl)\left(\sum_{\ell=1}^{N}\Phi_{k\ell}(S)(\Phi^{-1}(S))_{\ell k}\right)^{*}\cdot\,

In the preceding and all subsequent equations, the averages are evaluated over the distribution PΦ​(S)P_{\Phi}(S)  Eq. 11. Pulling out the inserted summation over ℓ\ell, the conjugated terms of the series now match the unconjugated terms. Then, after applying the identity Eq. 33 and pulling out the overall sign, both sets of terms are then given by a matrix minor of Φ⁡(S)\Phi(S) corresponding to removing row kk and an overlap with the state sks_{k}. The series over the NN-tuples SS can then be factorized into sum of the overlaps of sks_{k} and sum of the matrix minors over the other N−1N-1 states Sk¯S_{\overline{k}}. Thus, we get:

=1N!​det⁡[G]∑ℓ=1N∑S∈𝒮N(det[Φ(S)](Φ−1(S))ℓ​kΦk​ℓ(S))∗(det[Φ(S)](Φ−1(S))i​kAk​j(S))\displaystyle=\frac{1}{N!\det[G]}\sum_{\ell=1}^{N}\sum_{S\in\mathcal{S}^{N}}\biggl(\det[\Phi(S)]\,(\Phi^{-1}(S))_{\ell k}\,\Phi_{k\ell}(S)\biggl)^{*}\,\biggl(\det[\Phi(S)]\,(\Phi^{-1}(S))_{ik}\,A_{kj}(S)\biggl)
=1N!​det⁡[G]∑ℓ=1N∑S∈𝒮N((−1)k+ℓdet[(Φ(S))k¯​ℓ¯]Φk+ℓ(S))∗((−1)k+idet[(Φ(S))k¯​i¯]Ak​j(S))\displaystyle=\frac{1}{N!\det[G]}\sum_{\ell=1}^{N}\sum_{S\in\mathcal{S}^{N}}\biggl((-1)^{k+\ell}\det[\left(\,\Phi(S)\,\right)_{\overline{k}\overline{\ell}}]\,\Phi_{k+\ell}(S)\biggl)^{*}\,\biggl((-1)^{k+i}\det[\left(\,\Phi(S)\,\right)_{\overline{k}\overline{i}}]\,A_{kj}(S)\biggl)
=(−1)i+ℓN!​det⁡[G]∑ℓ=1N(∑Sk¯∈𝒮N−1det[Φℓ¯(Sk¯)]∗det[Φi¯(Sk¯)])(∑sk∈𝒮⟨ϕℓ|sk⟩⟨sk|aj⟩).\displaystyle=\frac{(-1)^{i+\ell}}{N!\det[G]}\sum_{\ell=1}^{N}\Biggl(\sum_{S_{\overline{k}}\in\mathcal{S}^{N-1}}\det[\Phi_{\overline{\ell}}(S_{\overline{k}})]^{*}\,\det[\Phi_{\overline{i}}(S_{\overline{k}})]\Biggl)\Biggl(\sum_{s_{k}\in\mathcal{S}}\langle\phi_{\ell}|s_{k}\rangle\langle s_{k}|a_{j}\rangle\Biggl).

The sums of sks_{k} overlaps result in the overlaps ⟨ϕℓ|aj⟩\langle\phi_{\ell}|a_{j}\rangle like for single state VMC averages, while the sums of matrix minors of Φ⁡(S)\Phi(S) over Sk¯S_{\overline{k}} from Eq. 34 result in the matrix minors of the Gram matrix G⁡(Φ)G(\Phi) with a factor of (N−1)!(N-1)!. Then, the matrix minor identity Eq. 33 is applied once again, but in reverse and in terms of the Gram matrix. So, the resulting matrix minors, the determinant from the partition function, and the composite sign from the original double application of the identity are transformed into inverse matrix elements. This leads to:

=(−1)i+ℓN!​det⁡[G]∑ℓ=1N((N−1)!det[Gℓ¯​i])(⟨ϕℓ|aj⟩)\displaystyle=\frac{(-1)^{i+\ell}}{N!\det[G]}\sum_{\ell=1}^{N}\biggl((N-1)!\,\det[G_{\overline{\ell}{i}}]\biggl)\biggl(\langle\phi_{\ell}|a_{j}\rangle\biggl)
=1N​∑ℓ=1N((−1)i+ℓ​det⁡[Gℓ¯​i¯]det⁡[G])​⟨ϕℓ|aj⟩=1N​∑ℓ=1N(G−1)i​ℓ​⟨ϕℓ|aj⟩\displaystyle=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{\ell=1}^{N}\left(\frac{(-1)^{i+\ell}\det[G_{\overline{\ell}\overline{i}}]}{\det[G]}\right)\,\langle\phi_{\ell}|a_{j}\rangle=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{\ell=1}^{N}(G^{-1})_{i\ell}\langle\phi_{\ell}|a_{j}\rangle
=1N​⟨ϕ~i|aj⟩.\displaystyle=\frac{1}{N}\langle\widetilde{\phi}_{i}|a_{j}\rangle.

The inserted summation over ℓ\ell from the first step transforms the inverse Gram matrix elements and the Φ\Phi basis overlaps with aja_{j} into a single dual basis overlap with aja_{j}. The normalization by a factor 1/N1/N arises from the factor of (N−1)!(N-1)! from the sums of matrix minors and the factor of N!N! from the partition function.

.3 Determinant Sampling Averages: Two Local Matrices

The averages for two local matrices can be expressed most clearly in terms of their sampling covariances. For the most general case of two ordered sets of states A=(a1,…,aN)A=(a_{1},\ldots,a_{N}) and B=(b1,…,bN)B=(b_{1},\ldots,b_{N}) with local matrices A~​(S)=Φ−1​(S)⋅A⁡(S)\widetilde{A}(S)=\Phi^{-1}(S)\cdot A(S) and B~​(S)=Φ−1​(S)⋅B⁡(S)\widetilde{B}(S)=\Phi^{-1}(S)\cdot B(S) respectively, their covariance expressed in terms of tensor products 𝔼⁡[A~†​(S)⊗B~​(S)]−𝔼⁡[A~​(S)]†⊗𝔼⁡[B~​(S′)]\Ex[\widetilde{A}^{\dagger}(S)\otimes\widetilde{B}(S)]-\Ex[\widetilde{A}(S)]^{\dagger}\otimes\Ex[\widetilde{B}(S^{\prime})] equates to the tensor product G−1⊗[[⁡A​|P^𝒱⟂|​B​]]G^{-1}\otimes\lbb A|\hat{P}_{\mathcal{V}^{\perp}}|B\rbb, but with respective indices permuted. Therefore, the covariance of each pair of individual local matrix elements specifically equates to

𝔼⁡[A~i1​j1∗​(S)​B~i2​j2​(S)]−𝔼⁡[A~i1​j1∗​(S)]​𝔼​[B~i2​j2​(S′)]=(G−1)i2​i1​⟨aj1|P^𝒱⟂|bj2⟩.\Ex\left[\widetilde{A}_{i_{1}j_{1}}^{*}(S)\,\widetilde{B}_{i_{2}j_{2}}(S)\right]-\Ex\left[\widetilde{A}_{i_{1}j_{1}}^{*}(S)\right]\Ex\left[\widetilde{B}_{i_{2}j_{2}}(S^{\prime})\right]=(G^{-1})_{i_{2}i_{1}}\,\langle a_{j_{1}}|\hat{P}_{\mathcal{V}^{\perp}}|b_{j_{2}}\rangle. (36)

As for operator expectation matrices, the sampling expression for operator covariance matrices Eq. 14 among operators A^\hat{A} and B^\hat{B} can be obtained for the case where |A]]=A^|Φ]]|A\rbb=\hat{A}|\Phi\rbb and similarly |B]]=B^|Φ]]|B\rbb=\hat{B}|\Phi\rbb. Contracting over the indices i1=j1i_{1}=j_{1} in the above equation then yields the matrix element Σ~i2​j2(A​B)\widetilde{\Sigma}^{(AB)}_{i_{2}j_{2}}.

Even more general sampling averages can be obtained for each of the individual terms after decomposing the local matrices as A~i1​j1​(S)=∑k1(Φ−1​(S))i1​k1​Ak1​j1​(S)\widetilde{A}_{i_{1}j_{1}}(S)=\sum_{k_{1}}(\Phi^{-1}(S))_{i_{1}k_{1}}A_{k_{1}j_{1}}(S) and B~i2​j2​(S)=∑k2(Φ−1​(S))i2​k2​Ak2​j2​(S)\widetilde{B}_{i_{2}j_{2}}(S)=\sum_{k_{2}}(\Phi^{-1}(S))_{i_{2}k_{2}}A_{k_{2}j_{2}}(S). The value of the averages for each combination of indices k1k_{1} and k2k_{2}, corresponding to the overlaps with the individual states sk1s_{k_{1}} and sk2s_{k_{2}} from the sampled NN-tuples SS respectively, is dependent on whether k1=k2k_{1}=k_{2} or k1≠k2k_{1}\neq k_{2}. Therefore, we obtain:

𝔼⁡[((Φ−1​(S))i1​k1​Ak1​j1​(S))∗​((Φ−1​(S))i2​k2​Bk2​j2​(S))]=\displaystyle\Ex\left[\left((\Phi^{-1}(S))_{i_{1}k_{1}}A_{k_{1}j_{1}}(S)\right)^{*}\,\left((\Phi^{-1}(S))_{i_{2}k_{2}}B_{k_{2}j_{2}}(S)\right)\right]=
1N​(G−1)i2​i1​⟨aj1|bj2⟩\displaystyle\frac{1}{N}(G^{-1})_{i_{2}i_{1}}\langle a_{j_{1}}|b_{j_{2}}\rangle for ​k1=k2\displaystyle\text{ for }k_{1}=k_{2}
1N⁡(N−1)​(⟨aj1|ϕ~i1⟩​⟨ϕ~i2|bj2⟩−(G−1)i2​i1​⟨aj1|P^𝒱|bj2⟩)\displaystyle\frac{1}{N(N-1)}\left(\langle a_{j_{1}}|\widetilde{\phi}_{i_{1}}\rangle\langle\widetilde{\phi}_{i_{2}}|b_{j_{2}}\rangle-(G^{-1})_{i_{2}i_{1}}\langle a_{j_{1}}|\hat{P}_{\mathcal{V}}|b_{j_{2}}\rangle\right) for ​k1≠k2\displaystyle\text{ for }k_{1}\neq k_{2}

The terms for the average of the NN k1=k2k_{1}=k_{2} combinations and the N⁡(N−1)N(N-1) k1≠k2k_{1}\neq k_{2} combinations are scaled by corresponding factors 1/N1/N and 1/N⁡(N−1)1/N(N-1) respectively. So, the average for the local matrix elements is the sum of the two terms for each case. The local matrix covariance Eq. 36 is thus formed combining the k1=k2k_{1}=k_{2} term, given by the overlap without the complementary projector P^𝒱⟂=1−P^𝒱\hat{P}_{\mathcal{V}^{\perp}}=1-\hat{P}_{\mathcal{V}} and the k1≠k2k_{1}\neq k_{2} and k1≠k2k_{1}\neq k_{2} term, given by the negative of the overlap with the projector P^𝒱\hat{P}_{\mathcal{V}} plus the subtracted averages 𝔼⁡[A~i1​j1∗​(S)]=⟨aj1|ϕ~i1⟩\Ex[\widetilde{A}_{i_{1}j_{1}}^{*}(S)]=\langle a_{j_{1}}|\widetilde{\phi}_{i_{1}}\rangle times 𝔼⁡[B~i2​j2​(S)]=⟨ϕ~i2|bj2⟩\Ex[\widetilde{B}_{i_{2}j_{2}}(S)]=\langle\widetilde{\phi}_{i_{2}}|b_{j_{2}}\rangle.

The derivation of the k1=k2=kk_{1}=k_{2}=k case follows essentially the same steps as the derivation for the single local matrix averages Eq. 35 in terms for BB and indices i2i_{2} and j2j_{2}. The only difference is that instead of inserting the identity 1=(Φ−1​(S)​Φ​(S))k​k∗1=(\Phi^{-1}(S)\Phi(S))_{kk}^{*}, those series of terms are replaced by the single term OPEN(Φ−1​(S))i1​k​Ak​j1​(S))∗(\Phi^{-1}(S))_{i_{1}k}A_{kj_{1}}(S))^{*}. This leads to:

Again, the primed indices denote what the unprimed indices become after the removal of another row/column index, so that k1′=k1k^{\prime}_{1}=k_{1} and k2′=k2−1k^{\prime}_{2}=k_{2}-1 if k1<k2k_{1}<k_{2} and k1′=k1−1k^{\prime}_{1}=k_{1}-1 and k2′=k2k^{\prime}_{2}=k_{2} if k1>k2k_{1}>k_{2}. The inserted summations over ℓ1\ell_{1} and ℓ2\ell_{2} are pulled out, and the indices ℓ1′\ell^{\prime}_{1} and ℓ2′\ell^{\prime}_{2} similarly denote the sub matrix indices for ℓ1\ell_{1} and ℓ2\ell_{2} after removing columns i1i_{1} and i2i_{2} respectively. As before, the conjugated and unconjugated terms are grouped and the identity Eq. 33 is applied to both. Each is then given individually by an overlap with sk1s_{k_{1}} an overlap with sk2s_{k_{2}} and a matrix minor of Φ⁡(S)\Phi(S) independent of both sk1s_{k_{1}} and sk2s_{k_{2}}. Then, the sums over the two overlaps with sk1s_{k_{1}} and the two overlaps with sk2s_{k_{2}} can both be factored out separately, with each resulting in a physical overlap. As before, the sum of the matrix minors over the remaining N−2N-2 states results in Gram matrix minors from Eq. 34 but now for (N−2)×(N−2)(N-2)\times(N-2) submatrices. The overall sign in the last line, given by the product of two signs (−1)i1+k1+ℓ1′+k2′(-1)^{i_{1}+k_{1}+\ell^{\prime}_{1}+k^{\prime}_{2}} and (−1)i2+k2+ℓ2′+k1′(-1)^{i_{2}+k_{2}+\ell^{\prime}_{2}+k^{\prime}_{1}} from the respective applications of the matrix minor identity, is denoted as ∓1\mp 1 as equals the negative of the ±1=(−1)i1+i2+ℓ1′+ℓ2′\pm 1=(-1)^{i_{1}+i_{2}+\ell^{\prime}_{1}+\ell^{\prime}_{2}} sign that will be eventually absorbed when the matrix minor identity is applied again on the Gram matrix minors, leaving an overall negative in the final result. Hence, it follows that:

=∓1N!​det⁡[G]∑ℓ1≠i1∑ℓ2≠i2(∑S(k1,k2)¯det[Φ(i1,ℓ1)¯(S(k1,k2)¯)]∗det[Φ(i2,ℓ2)¯(S(k1,k2)¯)])⋅\displaystyle=\frac{\mp 1}{N!\det[G]}\sum_{\ell_{1}\neq i_{1}}\sum_{\ell_{2}\neq i_{2}}\left(\sum_{S_{\overline{(k_{1},k_{2})}}}\det[\Phi_{\overline{(i_{1},\ell_{1})}}\left(S_{\overline{(k_{1},k_{2})}}\right)]^{*}\det[\Phi_{\overline{(i_{2},\ell_{2})}}\left(S_{\overline{(k_{1},k_{2})}}\right)]\right)\cdot

=−1N⁡(N−1)​∑ℓ1≠i1∑ℓ2≠i2(±det⁡[G(i1,ℓ1)¯​(i2,ℓ2)¯]det⁡[G])​⟨aj1|ϕℓ2⟩​⟨ϕℓ1|bj2⟩\displaystyle=\frac{-1}{N(N-1)}\sum_{\ell_{1}\neq i_{1}}\sum_{\ell_{2}\neq i_{2}}\left(\frac{\pm\det[G_{\overline{(i_{1},\ell_{1})}\overline{(i_{2},\ell_{2})}}]}{\det[G]}\right)\langle a_{j_{1}}|\phi_{\ell_{2}}\rangle\langle\phi_{\ell_{1}}|b_{j_{2}}\rangle
=−1N⁡(N−1)​∑ℓ1=1N∑ℓ2=1N(det⁡[(G−1)(i2,ℓ2)​(i1,ℓ1)])​⟨aj1|ϕℓ2⟩​⟨ϕℓ1|bj2⟩.\displaystyle=\frac{-1}{N(N-1)}\sum_{\ell_{1}=1}^{N}\sum_{\ell_{2}=1}^{N}\left(\det[(G^{-1})_{(i_{2},\ell_{2})(i_{1},\ell_{1})}]\right)\langle a_{j_{1}}|\phi_{\ell_{2}}\rangle\langle\phi_{\ell_{1}}|b_{j_{2}}\rangle.

The terms of the partition function are then incorporated. Firstly, the N!N! with the factor of (N−2)!(N-2)! from the redundant orderings in the sums of matrix minors gives the overall factor 1/N⁡(N−1)1/N(N-1). The Gram matrix determinant with the resulting Gram minors and ±1\pm 1 sign are transformed using the matrix minor identity into the inverse Gram matrix minors, now for 2×22\times 2 sub-matrices. In the last line, the summations over the inserted ℓ1\ell_{1} and ℓ2\ell_{2} indices are trivially extended to include ℓ1=i1\ell_{1}=i_{1} and ℓ2=i2\ell_{2}=i_{2} as all the added terms have matrix minors for selecting duplicate rows or columns, which are zero. This leads to:

=−1N⁡(N−1)​∑ℓ1=1N∑ℓ2=1N((G−1)i2​i1​(G−1)ℓ2​ℓ1−(G−1)i2​ℓ1​(G−1)ℓ2​i1)​⟨aj1|ϕℓ2⟩​⟨ϕℓ1|bj2⟩\displaystyle=\frac{-1}{N(N-1)}\sum_{\ell_{1}=1}^{N}\sum_{\ell_{2}=1}^{N}\left((G^{-1})_{i_{2}i_{1}}(G^{-1})_{\ell_{2}\ell_{1}}-(G^{-1})_{i_{2}\ell_{1}}(G^{-1})_{\ell_{2}i_{1}}\right)\langle a_{j_{1}}|\phi_{\ell_{2}}\rangle\langle\phi_{\ell_{1}}|b_{j_{2}}\rangle
=1N⁡(N−1)​(⟨aj1|ϕ~i1⟩​⟨ϕ~i2|bj2⟩−(G−1)i2​i1​⟨aj1|P^𝒱|bj2⟩).\displaystyle=\frac{1}{N(N-1)}\left(\langle a_{j_{1}}|\widetilde{\phi}_{i_{1}}\rangle\langle\widetilde{\phi}_{i_{2}}|b_{j_{2}}\rangle-(G^{-1})_{i_{2}i_{1}}\,\langle a_{j_{1}}|\hat{P}_{\mathcal{V}}|b_{j_{2}}\rangle\right).

Finally, the inverse Gram minors are expressed in terms of the individual inverse matrix elements. Contracting over all the ℓ1\ell_{1} and ℓ2\ell_{2} indices with the corresponding indices for Φ\Phi basis states in the overlaps again transforms them into Φ\Phi dual basis states. One of the terms can then be expressed in terms of the orthogonal projector P^𝒱=∑ℓ1|ϕ~ℓ1⟩​⟨ϕℓ1|=∑ℓ2|ϕℓ2⟩​⟨ϕ~ℓ2|\hat{P}_{\mathcal{V}}=\sum_{\ell_{1}}|\widetilde{\phi}_{\ell_{1}}\rangle\langle\phi_{\ell_{1}}|=\sum_{\ell_{2}}|\phi_{\ell_{2}}\rangle\langle\widetilde{\phi}_{\ell_{2}}|, eventually yielding Eq. 36.
